alex: Quick question — when a client sends both `model_id` and routing hints (e.g. `region:eu`, `tier:dedicated`), which parameter should win for selection? also: pin vs hint precedence?

maria: Short answer: we currently treat an explicit `model_id` as authoritative — hints only guide routing when `model_id` is absent. But note: there was a recent change around variant groups that makes this fuzzy for fallback behaviour.

kevin: Is that behaviour documented in the API contract? last I checked the contract said 'routing_hints are suggestions' but didn't enumerate interactions with `pin` or `model_variant`.

alex: Not explicitly, which is the problem. Clients are assuming hints can override in some edge cases (for region failover). We should be explicit: if `model_pin=true` then it must be honored, otherwise `model_id` wins and hints are used only for region/tier routing and selecting compatible variants.

sam: Proposal: precedence order — 1) explicit `model_pin` (if true, force exact model instance) 2) explicit `model_id` (select that model family/variant if compatible) 3) routing hints (`region`, `tier`, `pref_model_hint`) used to pick among compatible variants 4) fallback rules (tier downgrade, region fallback, cross-variant fallback).

maria: I like that. For backward compatibility, we should keep current default behaviour (model_id authoritative) and make `model_pin` opt-in so older clients won't break. Also add `served_model` and `fallback_reason` fields in the response to surface what was actually selected and why.

alex: Example request + response I'd like to standardize on (for the spec):

```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_id": "redwood-tts-v2",
  "routing_hints": {"region": "eu-west-1", "tier": "dedicated"},
  "model_pin": false
}
```

```
200 OK
{
  "id": "resp_...",
  "served_model": "redwood-tts-v2-quant-a",  // exact variant actually used
  "fallback_reason": "region-unavailable: routed to us-east-1; tier-matched:dedicated",
  "choices": [...] 
}
```

kevin: That `served_model` comment is important. Please make `served_model` the canonical string for auditing and billing. Also add `served_model_id` (the logical model family) if helpful — but don't nest objects, keep flat keys.

sam: One more compatibility edge: older clients set `routing_hints: {"region":"auto"}`. We should treat `auto` as client opt-in to cross-region routing; document that.

alex: Agreed. Action items: (1) I'll open a small API spec PR that adds `model_pin` (default false), documents precedence order, and shows the example responses. (2) @maria can you add a short note to the SDK changelog that `served_model` may appear in responses? (3) @kevin please review the PR for billing implications.

maria: ping me on the PR when it's up. Also we should add a unit test that asserts `served_model` is returned when `model_id` is present and region is forced.

kevin: I'll do a quick audit on usage meters if the shape changes.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/1287 — opened, contains spec + tests. cc @sam for canary plan.

ci-bot: CI passed for PR #1287 — 7 checks, 0 failures. :white_check_mark:

sam: For rollout, recommend canary in eu-west-1 for 24h with traffic mirroring for latency/billing checks, then global rollout. I'll draft a short runbook.

alex: Thanks everyone. If there are no objections by EOD I'll merge and coordinate SDK bumps. :thumbsup:

maria: No objections from me.

kevin: good from me too.
